```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid")
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.figsize": (10, 5), "axes.titleweight": "bold"})

data_path = Path("data/sales_data.csv")
if not data_path.exists():
    data_path = Path("../data/sales_data.csv")
if not data_path.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Could not find data/sales_data.csv. Render from the repository root "
        "or keep this report in the reports/ folder."
    )

sales = pd.read_csv(data_path, parse_dates=["order_date"])
required_columns = {
    "order_id", "order_date", "customer_id", "product_name", "category",
    "quantity", "total_price", "region", "sales_channel",
}
missing_columns = required_columns.difference(sales.columns)
if missing_columns:
    raise ValueError(f"The sales CSV is missing columns: {', '.join(sorted(missing_columns))}")

sales["year_month"] = sales["order_date"].dt.to_period("M").astype(str)
sales["year"] = sales["order_date"].dt.year
total_revenue = sales["total_price"].sum()
total_orders = sales["order_id"].nunique()
average_order_value = total_revenue / total_orders if total_orders else 0
unique_customers = sales["customer_id"].nunique()
units_sold = sales["quantity"].sum()

monthly = sales.groupby(["year", "year_month"], as_index=False).agg(
    revenue=("total_price", "sum"), orders=("order_id", "nunique")
)
category = sales.groupby("category", as_index=False).agg(
    revenue=("total_price", "sum"), orders=("order_id", "nunique"), units=("quantity", "sum")
).sort_values("revenue", ascending=False)
region = sales.groupby("region", as_index=False).agg(
    revenue=("total_price", "sum"), orders=("order_id", "nunique")
).sort_values("revenue", ascending=False)
channel = sales.groupby("sales_channel", as_index=False).agg(
    revenue=("total_price", "sum"), orders=("order_id", "nunique"), units=("quantity", "sum")
)
channel["average_order_value"] = channel["revenue"] / channel["orders"]
products = sales.groupby(["product_name", "category"], as_index=False).agg(
    revenue=("total_price", "sum"), units=("quantity", "sum"), orders=("order_id", "nunique")
).sort_values("revenue", ascending=False).head(10)
yearly = sales.groupby("year", as_index=False).agg(
    revenue=("total_price", "sum"), orders=("order_id", "nunique")
)
yearly["average_order_value"] = yearly["revenue"] / yearly["orders"]
```

## Executive summary

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    f"The dataset covers **{sales['order_date'].min():%Y-%m-%d} to "
    f"{sales['order_date'].max():%Y-%m-%d}** and contains **{len(sales):,}** "
    f"sales rows. Total revenue is **${total_revenue:,.0f}** across "
    f"**{total_orders:,}** orders, with an average order value of "
    f"**${average_order_value:,.2f}**.\n\n"
    f"The leading category is **{category.iloc[0]['category']}** "
    f"(${category.iloc[0]['revenue']:,.0f}). The highest-revenue region is "
    f"**{region.iloc[0]['region']}**, and **{channel.sort_values('revenue', ascending=False).iloc[0]['sales_channel']}** "
    "is the larger sales channel by revenue."
))
```

## Key performance indicators

```{python}
kpis = pd.DataFrame({

    "Value": [
        f"${total_revenue:,.2f}", f"{total_orders:,}", f"${average_order_value:,.2f}",

})
display(kpis.style.hide(axis="index"))
```

## Revenue over time

Monthly revenue shows how sales change across the available period. Compare the same months across years to distinguish year-to-year changes from seasonality.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
for year, group in monthly.groupby("year"):
    ax.plot(group["year_month"], group["revenue"], marker="o", linewidth=2, label=str(year))
ax.set(title="Monthly revenue", xlabel="Month", ylabel="Revenue ($)")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=60)
ax.legend(title="Year")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Annual comparison

```{python}
display(yearly.style.format({
    "revenue": "${:,.2f}", "orders": "{:,.0f}", "average_order_value": "${:,.2f}"
}).hide(axis="index"))
```

## Product and category performance

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
plot_category = category.sort_values("revenue")
ax.barh(plot_category["category"], plot_category["revenue"], color="#2563eb")
ax.set(title="Revenue by category", xlabel="Revenue ($)", ylabel="")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The table lists the ten highest-revenue products. Revenue describes value sold; units provide a complementary view of volume.

```{python}
display(products.style.format({"revenue": "${:,.2f}", "units": "{:,.0f}", "orders": "{:,.0f}"}).hide(axis="index"))
```

## Notes on interpretation

- The included data is synthetic and represents a simulated retail business.
- Every `order_id` is unique in this dataset; each row therefore represents one order. If the data changes to multiple line items per order, calculate order value by first summing line revenue per order.
- Revenue is the sum of `total_price`; average order value is revenue divided by distinct orders.
- This report reads `data/sales_data.csv` directly and does not require the SQLite database.
